Compare resident-creation permissions for Health Supervisor and PHN
Authorized administrator session and separate HS/PHN test accounts are available; inspect overrides through the approved UI.

1. Compare the default and effective permissions for HS and PHN.
2. Check whether resident-login creation appears for each role.
3. Verify the resulting action is allowed or denied according to the approved policy; do not save an unapproved override.
HS-SI-01, PHN-QA-01, resident R-TEST-007; San Isidro scope; permission view only unless policy authorizes a safe test.

Objective 3 — Health risk assessment and risk groups
Apply configured health-risk categories at and around threshold boundaries
Approved risk configuration and isolated synthetic vital-sign fixtures are available.

1. Enter synthetic values for configured categories.
2. Test each approved cutoff at one unit below, exactly at, and one unit above.
3. Compare the displayed classification with the approved configuration.
Resident R-TEST-012; VITAL-QA-01; use approved configured thresholds ±1 only; this tracker does not set clinical thresholds.
Values map consistently to the configured categories at, below, and above each cutoff across the triage and risk views.
Objective 3 — Health risk assessment and risk groups
Keep incomplete measurements separate from assessed risk groups
Synthetic residents with complete, partial, and missing measurements are available.

1. Review a complete fixture, a partial-vitals fixture, and a resident with no adequate measurements.
2. Compare each individual classification and the community distribution.
R-TEST-013 complete fixture; R-TEST-014 partial fixture; R-TEST-015 no adequate measurements.
Missing or insufficient inputs do not become Low risk by default. Residents without adequate measurements appear as Unassessed where supported.

2. Confirm the app shows a pending sync state.
3. Reconnect and sync, then retry once to check duplicate protection.

values: Functional Test Coverage by Core Module
Live counts from Manual Checklist. Results change when a test case status is updated.
Use Incomplete when a combined scenario has an unresolved check; use Blocked when access, environment, or data prevents execution.
Functional Test Results by Primary User Role
Each test case has one primary role so role totals reconcile to the overall case count.
Track functional test execution by core module and objective. The test cases include preconditions, repeatable steps, synthetic test data, expected results, and fields for actual outcomes.

Start on Module Summary, filter Manual Checklist by Core Module or Result, then execute one scenario using the listed synthetic data. Record actual behavior, date, tester, and reproducible defect details.

Pass = every check in the combined scenario passed. Fail = at least one check failed; include evidence. Incomplete = an attempted check needs work. Not tested = one or more checks remain unattempted. Blocked = access, environment, or data prevents execution.
All identities, accounts, households, services, reports, and clinical fixtures are fictional QA placeholders. Use an isolated non-production environment; never enter real resident health information.
Use only the system’s approved configuration or an approved synthetic fixture. This tracker does not prescribe clinical thresholds. Unexpected classifications require authorized clinical review.
Use authorized QA accounts and verify both interface and server-side restrictions. Do not change permissions outside an approved administrator workflow.

Objectives 1–6 align to centralized records, role-based access, risk assessment, notifications, reporting/analytics, and BHW visits/resident self-service. Cross-cutting cases cover mobile responsiveness and shared interface behavior.

The 38 scenarios combine overlapping workflows from the 145-case tracker. Combined from lists the prior KFG case IDs. Retired Cases lists removed setup, clinical-governance, migration-readiness, and engineering-only checks with the reason each is outside this functional suite.
Module Summary and Role Summary update automatically when Result changes. Primary User Role is the main execution owner; other roles involved in a workflow are named in the steps.
